scope: Existing evidence reuse only; no new external source retrieval in this pass.

claims.claim: Concrete household, work, animal and weather images invite figurative thinking.
claims.kind: Editorial reading of selected existing examples, not population-wide ethnography.
claims.support: Lemon overpressing, advice versus practice, and thunder versus rain show the transition from an image or contrast to conversational judgment.
claims.limits: No claim that every Odia household uses these or that they originated exclusively in Odisha.

claims.claim: Sayings can carry irony, complaint, reassurance or caution rather than one fixed moral.
claims.limits: Tone depends on context; not a claim of field-recorded conversations.

claims.claim: A dictionary note distinguishes rhymed dhaga from satirical dhamali.
claims.kind: Attributed terminology, bounded to this entry.
claims.limits: Do not turn this into an exhaustive universal genre boundary. Historical dictionary page independently verifying the digital transcription is pending.

claims.claim: A printed collection titled Dhagamalika was published in Cuttack in1893.
claims.locator: PDF1 title; lemon saying provisional historical witness printed2/PDF3 sixth text line, second saying.
claims.limits: Gobinda Rath is credited as publisher; no author substitution. Publication date is not an origin date. Incomplete transcription and unresolved reuse status remain.

claims.claim: Bibliographies and later compilations document a continuing record of collecting these expressions.
claims.limits: Optional background, not needed for short introduction. Does not independently establish oral transmission, exact wording, first origin or rights.

claims.claim: Ahimanikya Satapathy says he has lived away from Odisha for35years while the language has stayed with him.
claims.kind: Direct Founder testimony supplied in this conversation.
claims.limits: Keep first person and attributed to the author; do not generalise to every diaspora speaker or turn into a sourced population claim.

claims.claim: Ask children what they picture, when a saying might fit, and when it would be unfair.
claims.kind: Original editorial activity suggestion, not documented customary practice.
claims.limits: Use hypothetical everyday situations. Do not claim this is a traditional pedagogy or that a source prescribes these exercises.

claims.claim: Remembering a family version or discussing a different wording can open conversation.
claims.limits: A remembered version is testimony, not automatically a verified historical witness. No outreach or publication permission is implied.

claims.claim: Keeping a saying need not mean endorsing every old social assumption.
claims.kind: Editorial stance based on existing entry cautions.
claims.limits: Explain the image and context while retaining safeguards against disability/caste stereotyping, violence and inferred consent.
